items.title: Sam LaPorta (ankle) is not on the final injury report and will play in Week 12 against the Bears.
items.text: LaPorta began the week with a limited session before upgrading to full on Tuesday. The Lions’ No. 1 tight end should play a full complement of snaps in what will likely be a high-scoring game environment on Thursday. He should be in fantasy football lineups. - Nic Bodiford

items.title: Michael Pittman (foot) practiced in full on Wednesday.
items.text: Pittman is expected to return from injured reserve for Week 12 against the Broncos. Two full practices to open the week keep him on track to suit up on Friday. With Aaron Rodgers gone and the Steelers’ receiver room at full strength, Pittman will be a weak FLEX option if activated from IR. - Kyle Dvorchak

items.title: Rams activated DT Kobie Turner (groin) from injured reserve.
items.text: Turner missed a month while on IR because of the groin issue. He will be active tonight for a must-win game against the Packers. Turner made six starts this year. He has 22 combined tackles with two passbreakups. - Kyle Dvorchak

items.title: 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan said he thinks De’Zhaun Stribling (ankle) is “a couple of weeks away” from returning.
items.text: Exactly 10 weeks ago, it was reported that Stribling was expected to miss 10 weeks after undergoing surgery on his ankle. Unfortunately, it sounds like he needs more time to recover. ESPN’s Nick Wagoner believes Shanahan’s comments are in reference to Stribling “returning to practice, not necessarily playing.” Hopefully, Shanahan is actually referring to the latter timeframe. Regardless, Stribling should be stashed on fantasy football benches. - Nic Bodiford

items.title: Cowboys activated S Jalen Thompson (hamstring) from injured reserve.
items.text: Running back Jashaun Corbin was elevated from the practice squad. He will back up Javonte Williams tomorrow against the Eagles. Thompson is back in the lineup after suffering a hamstring injury in Week 3. He will provide a small boost to a defense that will need an offseason overhaul to meaningfully improve. - Kyle Dvorchak

items.title: Justin Herbert (concussion) did not practice on Wednesday.
items.text: Herbert was placed in the NFL’s concussion protocol following the Chargers’ Week 11 loss to the Jets. He took eight hits and six sacks that day. Herbert is firmly in the questionable camp at this time. His backup, DJ Uiagalelei, would only be a low-end QB2 against the Patriots if he gets the start this weekend. - Nic Bodiford

items.title: Panthers coach Dave Canales said he is optimistic that Tetairoa McMillan (foot) will play in Week 12 against the Bucs.
items.text: McMillan limped off the field in Week 11 with the foot issue but eventually returned to and finished the game. He did not practice today, though it’s not officially a DNP. The Panthers’ first practice of the week is tomorrow since they play on Monday, which will give McMillan an extra day to recover. Assuming all goes well in practice this week, McMillan will remain a fantasy WR2 for a must-win matchup with the Bucs. - Kyle Dvorchak

items.title: Ravens coach Jesse Minter said that Derrick Henry “had a couple of small symptoms” and is now in the NFL’s concussion protocol.
items.text: Minter adds that he expects Henry to play in Week 12 against the Texans. On Sunday, it was reported that Henry had cleared the concussion protocol after the Ravens’ Week 11 loss to the Panthers. Re-entering the concussion protocol mid-week seems like a bad sign. Justice Hill has played well in recent weeks and would presumably start in Henry’s stead if the burly back is unable to play. Hill is backed up by Rasheen Ali and rookie Adam Randall, the latter of whom could be worth adding in deep leagues. Henry was limited at practice today. - Nic Bodiford

items.title: The Pittsburgh Post-Gazette’s Gerry Dulac reports the Steelers are expected to release Aaron Rodgers.
items.text: The team announced his benching late Tuesday night. He then went on The Pat McAfee Show earlier today and burned every bridge in town by saying Mike McCarthy has been sleeping through meetings or missing them outright, among many other accusations. Per Dulac, the interview hastened Pittsburgh’s decision to get Rodgers off the roster. Once he clears waivers, Rodgers will be eligible to sign with another team. items.title: Mike Evans (Achilles) did not practice on Wednesday.
items.text: This is almost certainly just load management for the superstar wide receiver. Evans returned ot action last week, posting a 6/109/1 receiving line. He should be viewed as a talent- and volume-based WR2 against the Seahawks’ top-tier defense. Jordan Watkins (groin) will also sit out on Wednesday. - Nic Bodiford
